moduleTitle: Section 7 - Build Template and Link Values Recap
learningObjectives: Automate an end-to-end process, covering a more complicated use case.
Build a Template from a more advanced TestCase, leaving the correct References unresolved.
Link TestSheet Values, including buffered {MATH[]} calculations, to TestStepValues.
Use explicit Instance.Character conditions to select the intended generated paths and inspect their assertions.

elements.text: Independent hypothetical discount specification: one code waives shipping, another subtracts 5 from the total, and an invalid code must be rejected without applying a discount. Verify those outcomes against independent expected data. Current shop behavior and original Academy exercise instructions are not certified here.
Revisit the local Template, mapping and condition notes before attempting this combined independent practice.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: End-to-End Recap: Building a Working Template

elements.title: Plan, map, generate and verify
items: Prepare a focused TestCase with purposeful shared reuse.
Convert it to a Template and link the intended source.
Inspect XL paths and use generation conditions for the intended subset.
Check the model and generate or deliberately regenerate cases.
Trial-run the actual assertions and inspect logs; generation alone does not prove a working test.

elements.text: In this hypothetical model, Precondition_Reference and Order Product_Reference stay shared because no local changes are planned there. Resolve only the blocks that need a local editable variation. The names are examples, not a universal engine rule or verified course workspace layout.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Independent Practice: Expected Values and Timing

elements.text: Map the intended Attribute paths, preserving a composed Value only when its extra text is deliberate. Use a bounded WaitOn for the expected confirmation state before dependent steps, then verify the required business outcome. Allow Reorder enables rearranging TestStepValues; inspect execution dependencies before changing order. Buffer inputs before recall and review numeric interpretation/formatting when comparing monetary values. A displayed discount may be negative or a positive magnitude depending on the specification; do not enforce a universal leading minus.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Independent Practice: Select the Generated Paths

elements.text: Instance.Character != "Invalid" selects the non-invalid Character values, including Straight Through; it is not a lookup of named values Valid1/Valid2. Type an explicit supported property condition and inspect the resulting expression. Generation Conditions determine which steps exist, rather than jumping folders at runtime. In this hypothetical scenario, verify rejection and omit checkout for invalid codes, but keep every required assertion and cleanup step. Cleanup is not intrinsically invalid-only. Use && to combine clauses that must both hold. Resolve tab-match failures by inspecting browser, page state and identification before deciding to rescan.

Build with synthetic data and the local hypothetical specification. Original Academy exercise files, solution workspaces and figures were inaccessible; the local diagram and notes are independent aids, not reproduced official instructions.

examPitfalls.title: Generation does not prove correctness
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Calling a newly generated model a successful test without execution.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect generated subsets and trial-run their assertions.

examPitfalls.title: Keep purposeful reuse
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Resolving every shared block irrespective of planned edits.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Resolve only a deliberate local variation.

examPitfalls.title: Character is not a named data value
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating Valid1 as a Character or treating non-invalid as only Valid.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Character supports Valid, Invalid and Straight Through.

examPitfalls.title: Cleanup follows the specification
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming only invalid input ever needs cleanup.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Provide required cleanup and assertions on every intended path.

examPitfalls.title: Identification needs diagnosis
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Automatically rescanning on any missing-tab error.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect the loaded page, browser and stable unique identifiers first.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which ordered workflow builds a data-driven Template and validates its generated tests?

options.text: Create the ExecutionList → Link RequirementSet → Convert to Template → Add Conditions.
Create the TestSheet → Instantiate → Convert to Template → Add Conditions.
Prepare TestCase, convert, link data/paths, set intended conditions, check/generate, then trial-run assertions.
Add Conditions → Create the TestCase → Link Values → Convert to Template.

practiceQuiz.hint: TestCase and TestSheet come first; Conditions and Instantiation come last.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Generation depends on the model and mappings; trial execution separately checks actual outcomes.

optionExplanations.A: Execution setup before the model does not provide its data mappings.
optionExplanations.B: A plain TestCase cannot be instantiated as a Template before conversion.
optionExplanations.C: This orders model preparation, mapping, generation and separate execution checks.
optionExplanations.D: Conditions and mappings need an appropriate model and source.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Instance Character denotes input that the business process is expected to reject?

options.text: A green circle.
A blue square with a 'T'.
A red exclamation mark.
Invalid

practiceQuiz.hint: This is a business-data Character, not a test-result status.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Invalid Character indicates an expected error for that input; a correct negative test can pass.

optionExplanations.A: A color description is not the Character value requested.
optionExplanations.B: The Template type marker does not define input validity.
optionExplanations.C: An error indicator is not the Character property value.
optionExplanations.D: Invalid denotes input expected to trigger a business error.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which property condition selects all non-invalid Characters, including Straight Through, for generation?

options.text: 'Instance.Character' == "Valid1" OR == "Valid2" OR == "Valid3" (one per valid code)
'Instance.Character' != "Invalid"
No condition — always run both folders regardless of validity.
'Discount.Code' == ""

practiceQuiz.hint: One readable condition covering all valid cases, using the != operator.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The condition excludes Invalid and therefore includes both Valid and Straight Through; it selects generated structure rather than making runtime jumps.

optionExplanations.A: Valid1/Valid2 are not the documented Character enum values.
optionExplanations.B: Inequality excludes Invalid, including the other supported Characters.
optionExplanations.C: Unconditional inclusion also keeps the unwanted invalid workflow.
optionExplanations.D: An empty code comparison is not a Character-validity condition.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The independent specification says to verify rejection, omit checkout and perform cleanup after an invalid code. Which generated path fits?

options.text: Include the rejection assertions and required cleanup while omitting the checkout workflow.
The TestCase should restart from the beginning.
The TestCase should continue through the full checkout process anyway.
The TestCase should pause and wait for manual input.

practiceQuiz.hint: There's no need to keep testing an order that's already been correctly rejected.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Select the required negative assertions and cleanup, not unrelated checkout steps. This follows the stated independent specification.

optionExplanations.A: This retains the specified rejection assertions and cleanup while omitting checkout.
optionExplanations.B: Restarting is not required by this specification.
optionExplanations.C: Checkout contradicts the stated rejected-order path.
optionExplanations.D: A manual pause is not the specified automated outcome.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the independent model, Precondition_Reference and Order Product_Reference require no local changes. Which blocks should remain shared?

options.text: Checkout Process and Confirmation.
Precondition_Reference and Order Product_Reference.
Verification of Prices and Verification of Success.
Every folder must be resolved — none stay as References.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Keep the two unmodified shared blocks referenced. Their example names do not create a universal resolution rule.

optionExplanations.A: Those checkout blocks were not the two declared unchanged shared blocks.
optionExplanations.B: The two unchanged shared blocks can remain referenced.
optionExplanations.C: Those verification blocks were not declared as the unchanged pair.
optionExplanations.D: Templates support references; resolving every block is unnecessary.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A confirmation state may arrive after a delay. Why use a bounded WaitOn before dependent operations?

options.text: Wait for the specified state within the configured timeout before continuing.
So Tosca skips the verification entirely.
So the TestStep runs twice.
WaitOn has no effect on verification TestSteps.

practiceQuiz.hint: The message may take a moment to render after the code is submitted.
practiceQuiz.rationale: WaitOn waits for a specified state within a timeout; it does not guarantee success or replace all later assertions.

optionExplanations.A: Bounded state-based waiting handles the described timing dependency.
optionExplanations.B: WaitOn does not mean discard the required verification.
optionExplanations.C: It does not define a repeat count of two.
optionExplanations.D: WaitOn is specifically useful for synchronization with the expected state.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What must you do before you can rearrange the TestStepValues under "Verification of Prices"?

options.text: Right-click the TestStep and select Allow Reorder.
Delete and recreate the TestStep.
Set the WorkState to COMPLETED.
Nothing — TestStepValues can always be freely reordered.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a right-click context menu option on the TestStep itself.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TestStepValues can only be rearranged after enabling Allow Reorder via the TestStep's right-click context menu.

optionExplanations.A: Allow Reorder enables the intended Value rearrangement.
optionExplanations.B: Deleting the step is unnecessary to enable order changes.
optionExplanations.C: WorkState does not enable this order operation.
optionExplanations.D: The documented option controls whether values can be rearranged.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How do you define a conditional-instantiation expression based on the Instance Character property?

options.text: Enter and inspect an explicit expression such as Instance.Character != "Invalid".
Because Instance.Character conditions are deprecated in Tosca.
Because it can only be set on TestStepValues, never on TestStepFolders.
Because it requires a separate license.

practiceQuiz.hint: Use the supported property path, not a claim about every possible editing gesture.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The documented Instance-prefixed Character property can be referenced in a condition. Its semantics differ from one named Attribute Instance.

optionExplanations.A: This uses the documented Instance property condition syntax.
optionExplanations.B: Instance.Character is supported rather than deprecated here.
optionExplanations.C: Condition targets include folders, not only individual values.
optionExplanations.D: No separate Character-condition license is documented.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The independent negative-test specification requires an Empty Shopping Cart cleanup folder only for Invalid combinations. Which generation condition matches that stated scope?

options.text: 'Instance.Character' == "Invalid" — so the cart is only emptied after an invalid code was entered and rejected.
'Instance.Character' != "Invalid" — so the cart is only emptied for valid codes.
No Condition — the cart should always be emptied regardless of code validity.
'Workflow.Discount Type' == "Discount Type Flat".

practiceQuiz.hint: This is the opposite of the Condition used on Checkout Process, Verification of Prices, Confirmation, and Verification of Success.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The equality condition selects Invalid combinations for the cleanup scope specified here. This is not a universal claim that valid tests never need cleanup.

optionExplanations.A: Equality selects Invalid for the explicitly stated cleanup scope.
optionExplanations.B: Inequality selects the other Characters and misses the specified Invalid scope.
optionExplanations.C: Unconditional cleanup includes more paths than this specification requests.
optionExplanations.D: Discount type does not express the stated Character scope.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An API-independent UI test cannot find its target browser tab. Which is a responsible first investigation?

options.text: Inspect browser selection, navigation/page state and the Module’s stable unique tab identifiers; rescan only when needed.
The license has expired — contact Tricentis support.
The TestSheet is linked to the wrong Template — delete and relink it.
The ExecutionList folder is missing — recreate it.

practiceQuiz.hint: Diagnose the current match before rebuilding the model.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A missing match does not by itself prove instability or a license failure. Check the target state and identifiers before rescan.

optionExplanations.A: This inspects the actual target state and identification before changing the model.
optionExplanations.B: A missing tab is not proof that a license expired.
optionExplanations.C: Deleting a data link does not address browser-tab identification.
optionExplanations.D: An ExecutionList folder does not identify the current browser tab.

quickRecap.value: Prepare, map, condition, check, generate and separately trial-run.
Non-invalid includes both Valid and Straight Through.
Follow the stated path specification; valid paths may also need cleanup.
Use bounded WaitOn for the specified state, not as proof of all outcomes.
Inspect target state and unique stable identifiers before rescan.
